topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the overarching focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate pathogen and damage recognition mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular strategies and receptor systems used by the innate immune system to detect microbial presence and cellular damage.

topics.label: Inflammatory response execution, cell trafficking, and systemic effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cells initiate local leukocyte extravasation, lymphatic antigen transport, and the systemic consequences of escalating inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammatory states
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the mechanisms required to terminate acute inflammation, rebuild damaged tissue, and manage unresolved or chronic inflammatory conditions.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture and indicates the topic of the subsequent session.
